legend: There is an extensive mixed inflammatory infiltrate; this example includes plasma cells, eosinophils, and histiocytes, along with prominent neutrophils. The tumour architecture is completely obscured, with only scattered atypical neoplastic stromal cells discernible.

Lobules of adipocytes of mature appearance are intersected by variable fibrous septa, within which are scattered atypical spindle cells with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei. These atypical cells can typically be seen at low magnification.

diagnosis: Lipoma-like atypical lipomatous tumour / well-differentiated liposarcoma
legend: Although variable numbers of lipoblasts may be seen, their presence does not make, and is not required for, a diagnosis of atypical lipomatous tumour / well-differentiated liposarcoma.

This non-lipogenic area within well-differentiated liposarcoma shows prominent atypical, hyperchromatic spindle cells in collagenous stroma. Cellularity is at most moderate, and mitotic figures are lacking.

Atypical stromal spindle cells are present in an extensive, sparsely cellular fibrillary collagenous background. Only occasional mature adipocytes are present. The fibrous component can overshadow lipogenic areas of the neoplasm, such that these are missed in small samples.

diagnosis: CDK4 immunohistochemistry, atypical lipomatous tumour / well-differentiated liposarcoma
legend: There is diffuse, strong nuclear CDK4 expression within both stromal spindle cells and lipoblasts.

Axial contrast-enhanced CT scan demonstrating abnormal retroperitoneal fat (asterisk), which is displacing the bowel anteriorly. The mass shows bland fat attenuation with no soft tissue elements to suggest dedifferentiation. Coarse calcifications are noted medially within the mass (arrow).
